It seems like there are currently three major "types" of questions asked on AskVoat. First, there are the discussion-oriented questions (similar to the AskReddit community) that seem to best fit this particular community. A good example is this post currently sitting near the top of the subverse.

The second type of question I've been seeing are those intended to start a discussion about Voat and its features in particular, such as this one. While these questions aren't nearly as open-ended and have (in my opinion) less potential to start interesting discussions, I feel that AskVoat is probably the most appropriate place for these types of questions unless there is some meta Voat discussion subverse I am unaware of.

The third type of question, however, are people asking for advice or answers to really specific questions. A good example would be this post currently at the top of the subverse. While there is nothing inherently wrong with these questions, they are not intended to encourage discussion, and therefore I feel that an individual subverse for asking advice-related questions is in order.

Thoughts?

EDIT: From the responsive I've received so far, it sounds like there are a couple of options for advice-type questions here on Voat. I guess my suggestion now would be that the moderators of this subverse set some clearer guidelines about what types of questions are most appropriate for this sub, redirecting other questions to more appropriate subverses such as v/nostupidquestions and v/dearabby (thanks u/TheMidnightBum and u/walkernaught)

Android and Windows should embrace RAW photography before Apple catches up

As an advanced amateur photographer, I was all excited for RAW on my N6. I bought a fancy camera app, but then realized the HDR in the stock camera app was more than enough for me. When my phone is out, I don't need a DSLR replacement, I need quick photos. I could take or leave RAW support honestly.

I think I agree with in in that I don't really think a phone camera needs RAW support as most of the time if I want to take a nicer picture than a quick snap I would take it on a small compact like my X100T. I also think the problem is non-photographers will turn it on and wonder why all their photos are flat and unsharp as somewhere on the internet they will hear that if they don't use RAW they aren't getting the most out of their camera.

And then wonder why they can't see the pictures on Facebook because they didn't export JPG. Phone cameras should follow the KISS method here. People who would use it probably already have a camera anyway.
Android now has the camera2 API that comes with Lollipop, so the underlying system infrastructure is there, It's just up to manufacturers to include it in their OEM apps.
